transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Riya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Pulse Labs CTO), Lena Ortiz (Pulse Labs Lead ML Eng), Marcus Wu (Pulse Labs Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick discovery for Pulse Labs evaluating Redwood's PLG quickstart (hosted API) with potential to move to Dedicated or Private in Q3 if SLOs and compliance checks pass. Focus: time-to-first-token, free credits, onboarding steps, and benchmarking requirements.

Topics:
- Quickstart and free credits flow
- Time-to-first-token and SDKs
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching, KV cache hints
- Dedicated pool questions (throughput/commit)
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, VPC/private deploy

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Hayes from Redwood, with Riya our solutions eng. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Samir: Good, thanks. Excited to chat, we've been poking around the quickstart docs and wanted to understand how fast we can get up and running.
[00:00:15] Jordan: Totally. Real quick agenda — go over the PLG quickstart, show how free credits and account setup works, call out time-to-first-token, then Riya will cover integrations and benchmarking for dedicated.
[00:00:27] Lena: Sounds good. Our main goal is to get something in prod for an internal assistant by end of Q2, but first we need to validate latency and cost.
[00:00:35] Riya: Great. For the hosted API quickstart, typical flow is sign up, claim credits, API key in Console, run the sample curl or SDK snippet — from sign-up to a token in many cases under 10 minutes if you have SSO off.
[00:00:48] Marcus: When you say "token" you mean first model response? What's the typical end-to-end?
[00:00:53] Riya: Right, first model response. Realistically 2-8 minutes if you follow the quickstart, longer if your org needs SSO or has IP allowlists. We have SDKs in Python/Node and a one-file quickstart repo.
[00:01:05] Samir: Cool. Can you walk through credit redemption — any limits or expiration?
[00:01:10] Jordan: Free credits are time-limited (90 days on the current promotion) and bound to the account. They apply to hosted API usage only; dedicated trial is a separate evaluation. We can extend in pilot cases — discuss after you start.
[00:01:22] Lena: Important for us: data retention and logs. We need to ensure no customer PII is retained in hosted during evaluation.
[00:01:28] Riya: Understood. Hosted by default doesn't persist prompt content beyond short-term logs used for debugging; there are controls for log redaction, and we offer Private deployments or Dedicated with data isolation if you need stricter retention. We have SOC 2 artifacts.
[00:01:40] Marcus: Can you share those docs? We have a security checklist to satisfy.
[00:01:43] Jordan: Yes, we'll send the SOC 2 report and a security bundle — I'll put that in the next-steps.
[00:01:49] [00:02:00] Samir: On the performance side, our internal SLO is p95 <= 250ms for short prompts (up to 256 tokens). How do you think hosted performs?
[00:02:08] Riya: Hosted can hit low latency for small models and short sequences, but for consistent p95 under 250ms at scale we'd usually recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity. However, for initial validation, you'll see p50/p95 in the 100-300ms range depending on model and region — we have perf profiles per model in the catalog.
[00:02:26] Lena: Does Redwood do KV cache/prefix caching for chat use cases? We have long conversations and want cheaper token costs for repeated context.
[00:02:33] Riya: Yes — the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated compute for the same context; that works both on hosted and in Dedicated. On hosted it's automatic heuristics; Dedicated gives you more tuning knobs and observability.
[00:02:47] Marcus: About cost — can you give a ballpark between hosted per-token and Dedicated commit?
[00:02:52] Jordan: Ballpark: hosted per-token can be cheaper for low steady-state if you keep models small and use batching/caching. Dedicated becomes more economical at higher throughput; commitments reduce unit price but require a monthly/annual commit. We'll send you a simple cost worksheet.
[00:03:05] Samir: Any gotchas with quantized models vs fp16 for accuracy?
[00:03:09] Riya: There's a tradeoff — 4-bit quantized usually keeps quality high for many inference tasks, but certain instruction-following workloads see regressions. We recommend running small evals using your prompts — the quickstart includes an eval harness to compare quality.
[00:03:22] [00:03:30] Lena: We use GCP in us-central1, any region constraints?
[00:03:33] Jordan: Hosted has region coverage; Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions. For private on-prem or VPC, we can ship a package or integrate with customer VPC peering.
[00:03:44] Marcus: If we start with hosted and later move to Dedicated, what's the migration story?
[00:03:48] Riya: The API is consistent — same endpoints and SDKs. You can pin model versions and rollout policies. For traffic routing, there's an abstraction layer so migrating is mostly config and capacity planning. We do canary rollouts to validate.
[00:04:00] Samir: Nice. Next, about security — KMS for key management and audit logs?
[00:04:04] Riya: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer KMS/HSM integration and detailed audit logs. Hosted supports KMS for encryption at rest, with additional controls on enterprise plans.
[00:04:15] [00:04:30] Lena: For the quickstart, can we run a throughput test — e.g., 100 concurrent streams — or will rate limits block us?
[00:04:36] Jordan: Hosted has default rate limits to protect service and new accounts; we can lift limits for pilots. For realistic throughput tests, we usually spin up a dedicated trial or simulate traffic with a SE-managed benchmark. Riya can coordinate.
[00:04:50] Riya: I'll prepare a benchmark checklist: target concurrency, payload sizes, model selection, and evaluation prompts. That'll make the dedicated trial efficient.
[00:04:58] Marcus: Good. On observability, we want per-token cost breakdown and traces; do you expose that?
[00:05:03] Riya: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analytics. For Dedicated you get longer retention windows and more granular telemetry.
[00:05:14] Samir: A couple of trade-off questions — latency vs cost and batching. If we increase batching, we save cost but increase tail latency, right?
[00:05:22] Riya: Exactly. There's a balance: continuous batching improves throughput/cost but can hurt latency SLOs. We can tune batching profiles per route. Also prefix caching and request routing to faster model variants help.
[00:05:33] [00:05:45] Lena: For our assistant we expect a mix of short prompts (quick answers) and longer generation for summaries. The longer ones can be async. Any recommendations?
[00:05:53] Riya: Split workloads by route: sync short-prompt route optimized for low latency, longer async generation on a different queue with higher throughput. You can assign different models or quantization profiles per route.
[00:06:06] Marcus: How does function/tool calling work? We're hoping to plug into our existing toolchain.
[00:06:09] Jordan: We support function/tool calling primitives with structured output support. It's in the SDK; Riya can show a quick example in the onboarding session.
[00:06:19] [00:06:30] Samir: Any mention of competitors from your customers? We're also looking at Anthropic and OpenAI for evals.
[00:06:34] Jordan: That's common. We often show perf and cost cards against them — mainly around latency for on-prem and cost for high throughput. We'll be transparent about tradeoffs.
[00:06:45] Lena: For the quickstart, what's the typical success criteria you track in pilots?
[00:06:50] Riya: Usually: integration done in <2 weeks, p95 latency target met for core route, cost per 1k tokens within expected range, and no unresolved security blockers. If those are met, customers often commit to Dedicated or Private planning.
[00:07:02] [00:07:15] Marcus: Any SDK gotchas — auth rotation, key management?
[00:07:19] Riya: We recommend short-lived keys for automation with rotation via your secrets manager; the SDK supports that pattern. We'll include examples for HashiCorp Vault and GCP Secret Manager.
[00:07:30] Samir: Great. Let's talk timeline — we want an internal demo by end of May and a pilot in June. Is that feasible?
[00:07:38] Jordan: Yes, start with hosted quickstart now, claim credits, run initial evals in May. If benchmarks look good, we'll scope a Dedicated pilot for June.
[00:07:47] Lena: For the hosted quickstart, do we need any network changes?
[00:07:50] Riya: No for basic hosted API, just outbound calls to the API endpoint. For Private or VPC peering we'll need networking details.
[00:07:59] [00:08:15] Marcus: Do you support SAML SSO for Console access?
[00:08:18] Jordan: Yes — enterprise accounts can enable SAML/SSO and RBAC. For PLG quickstart you can start without SSO and enable later.
[00:08:27] Samir: Ok. Can you outline the exact next steps so we can take back to the team?
[00:08:31] Jordan: Sure — 1) we'll send quickstart link + claim-credit steps and the sample repo; 2) SOC 2/security bundle; 3) Riya will send benchmark checklist and we'll schedule a 60-min SE demo the week of 4/26; 4) Jordan to follow up with ballpark Dedicated pricing.
[00:08:49] [00:09:00] Lena: Perfect. Any obstacles we should watch out for?
[00:09:03] Riya: Main things: ensure your prompt set for evals reflects production patterns; check tokenization expectations; and if you need sub-250ms p95, prepare to test on Dedicated.
[00:09:16] Marcus: For the benchmarks, can you provide a starter prompt set?
[00:09:19] Riya: Yes, we'll include a sample prompt set and the eval harness in the quickstart repo.
[00:09:25] Samir: Alright, thanks. That helps. Let's wrap with the timelines and who owns what.
[00:09:30] Jordan: I'll capture action items in the follow-up. Riya, anything to add?
[00:09:35] Riya: Just that we'll try to keep the hosted friction minimal — we'll also note how to request lifted rate-limits for pilot traffic.
[00:09:42] [00:10:00] Samir: One more question on data residency — we have EU customers, do you support region-specific retention?
[00:10:07] Jordan: Yes, region-specific deployments are possible — hosted will route by region, and Private or Dedicated can meet stricter residency requirements. We'll include region support matrix in the doc pack.
[00:10:19] Lena: Excellent. That should cover it for now.
[00:10:22] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll send the bundle and follow up with proposed times for the SE demo.
[00:10:28] Samir: Thanks — appreciate it.

(Transcript continues with Q&A and clarifications; meeting ends around 15:45 UTC)

Notes on transcription: auto-generated captions had minor misrecognitions around product names (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache") and occasional speaker attribution glitches. Some timestamps were inferred post-call.
